statement0:
The word "perceptual" is mentioned two or more times in 0.9% of psychology papers' Results sections, as of 2020-2024.

Among 2020-2024 papers containing "perceptual" , 25.3% of reported significant p-values (p < .05) are fragile (.01 ≤ p < .05) - i.e., barely fall under the standard significance threshold. This is a lower rate than the median Psychology paper (median shown for reference); relative to other words, papers with "perceptual" are in the bottom 24th percentile of fragile p-value percentages (lower = better). Note, strong/weak p-values highly predict replicability.
statement1: As of 2020-2024, papers containing "perceptual" tend to be published in lower impact factor journals (5th percentile among all words) and tend to be cited less (1st percentile word). In general, this word is positively associated with university ranking, such that higher-ranked institutions are more likely to publish papers containing "perceptual" (93rd percentile).
